<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">EMPLOYEE STOCK OWNERSHIP PLAN:</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company established an Employee Stock Ownership Plan (ESOP) as part of its stock issuance on November&nbsp;19, 2012.&#160; The ESOP is accounted for in accordance with ASC 718-40, &#147;Compensation &#151; Stock Compensation &#151; Employee Stock Ownership Plan.&#148;&#160; Under ASC 718-40, unearned ESOP shares are not considered outstanding and are therefore not taken into account when computing earnings per share.&#160; Unearned ESOP shares are presented as a reduction to stockholders&#146; equity and represent shares to be allocated to ESOP participants in future periods for services provided by the Company.&#160; As shares are committed to be released, compensation expense is recognized for the fair market value of the stock and stockholders&#146; equity is increased by a corresponding amount.&#160; The loan to the ESOP will be repaid principally from the Bank&#146;s contributions to the ESOP over a period of 6.1 years.&#160; See Note 11.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">RECENT ACCOUNTING PRONOUNCEMENTS:</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In January&nbsp;2014, the Financial Accounting Standards Board (FASB) issued Accounting Standards Update (ASU) 2014-01, &#147;Investments &#151; Equity Method and Joint Ventures (Topic 323): Accounting for Investments in Qualified Affordable Housing Projects.&#148; The amendments in this ASU apply to all reporting entities that invest in qualified affordable housing projects through limited liability entities that are flow-through entities for tax purposes as follows:</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="font-size:10.0pt;margin:0in 0in .0001pt 1.0in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">1.</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font>For reporting entities that meet the conditions for and that elect to use the proportional amortization method to account for investments in qualified affordable housing projects, all amendments in this ASU apply.</p>
<p style="font-size:10.0pt;margin:0in 0in .0001pt 1.0in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">2.</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font>For reporting entities that do not meet the conditions for or that do not elect the proportional amortization method, only the amendments in this ASU that are related to disclosures apply.</p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The amendments in this ASU permit reporting entities to make an accounting policy election to account for their investments in qualified affordable housing projects using the proportional amortization method if certain conditions are met.&#160; Under the proportional amortization method, an entity amortizes the initial cost of the investment in proportion to the tax credits and other tax benefits received and recognizes the net investment performance in the income statement as a component of income tax expense (benefit).&#160; For those investments in qualified affordable housing projects not accounted for using the proportional amortization method, the investment should be accounted for as an equity method investment or a cost method investment in accordance with Subtopic 970-323.&#160; The amendments in this ASU should be applied retrospectively to all periods presented.&#160; A reporting entity that uses the effective yield method to account for its investments in qualified affordable housing projects before the date of adoption may continue to apply the effective yield method for those preexisting investments.&#160; The amendments in this ASU are effective for public business entities for annual periods and interim reporting periods within those annual periods, beginning after December&nbsp;15, 2014.&#160; Early adoption is permitted.&#160; The Company does not expect that the adoption of this ASU will have an impact on the Company&#146;s consolidated financial statements.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In January&nbsp;2014, the FASB issued ASU 2014-04, &#147;Receivables-Troubled Debt Restructurings by Creditors (Subtopic 310-40):&#160; Reclassification of Residential Real Estate Collateralized Consumer Mortgage Loans upon Foreclosure.&#148;&#160; The objective of the amendments in this ASU is to reduce diversity by clarifying when an in substance repossession or foreclosure occurs, that is, when a creditor should be considered to have received physical possession of residential real estate property collateralizing a consumer mortgage loan such that the loan receivable should be derecognized and the real estate property recognized.&#160; The amendments in this ASU clarify that an in substance repossession or foreclosure occurs, and a creditor is considered to have received physical possession of residential real estate property collateralizing a consumer mortgage loan, upon either (1)&nbsp;the creditor obtaining legal title to the residential real estate property upon completion of a foreclosure or (2)&nbsp;the borrower conveying all interest in the residential real estate property to the creditor to satisfy that loan through completion of a deed in lieu of foreclosure or through a similar legal agreement.&#160; Additionally, the amendments require interim and annual disclosure of</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p align="center" style="font-size:10.0pt;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">F-</font>14<a name="PB_14_152348_5891"></a></p>
<div style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><hr size="3" width="100%" noshade align="left" style="color:#010101;"></div>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">both (1)&nbsp;the amount of foreclosed residential real estate property held by the creditor and (2)&nbsp;the recorded investment in consumer mortgage loans collateralized by residential real estate property that are in the process of foreclosure according to local requirements of the applicable jurisdiction.&#160; The amendments in this ASU are effective for public business entities for annual periods, and interim periods within those annual periods, beginning after December&nbsp;15, 2014.&#160; An entity can elect to adopt the amendments in this ASU using either a modified retrospective transition method or a prospective transition method.&#160; The Company does not expect that the adoption of this ASU will have a material impact on the Company&#146;s consolidated financial statements.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In April&nbsp;2014, the FASB issued ASU 2014-08, &#147;Presentation of Financial Statements (Topic 205) and Property, Plant, and Equipment (Topic 360):&#160; Reporting Discontinued Operations and Disclosures of Disposals of Components of an Entity.&#148;&#160; This ASU changes the criteria for reporting discontinued operations and modifies related disclosure requirements.&#160; The new guidance is effective within annual periods beginning on or after December&nbsp;15, 2014, and interim periods within those years.&#160; The adoption of this guidance is not expected to have a material impact on the Company&#146;s consolidated financial statements.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In May&nbsp;2014, the FASB issued ASU 2014-09, &#147;Revenue from Contracts with Customers (Topic 606).&#148;&#160; The objective of this ASU is to clarify principles for recognizing revenue and to develop a common revenue standard for GAAP and International Financial Reporting Standards.&#160; The guidance in this ASU affects any entity that either enters into contracts with customers to transfer goods or services or enters into contracts for the transfer of nonfinancial assets unless those contracts are within the scope of other standards.&#160; The core principal of the guidance is that an entity should recognize revenue to depict the transfer of promised goods or services to customers in an amount that reflects the consideration to which the entity expects to be entitled in exchange for those goods or services.&#160; The amendments in this update are effective for annual reporting periods beginning after December&nbsp;15, 2016, including interim periods within that reporting period.&#160; Early application is not permitted.&#160; The Company is currently reviewing this ASU to determine if it will have an impact on its consolidated financial statements.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In June&nbsp;2014, the FASB issued ASU 2014-11, &#147;Transfers and Servicing (Topic 860):&#160; Repurchase-to-Maturity Transactions, Repurchase Financings, and Disclosures.&#148;&#160; The amendments in this ASU require two accounting changes.&#160; First, the amendments in this ASU change the accounting for repurchase-to-maturity transactions to secured borrowing accounting.&#160; Second, for repurchase financing arrangements, the amendments require separate accounting for a transfer of a financial asset executed contemporaneously with a repurchase agreement with the same counterparty, which will result in secured borrowing accounting for the repurchase agreement.&#160; This ASU also includes new disclosure requirements.&#160; The accounting changes in this Update are effective for the first interim or annual period beginning after December&nbsp;15, 2014.&#160; An entity is required to present changes in accounting for transactions outstanding on the effective date as a cumulative-effect adjustment to retained earnings as of the beginning of the period of adoption.&#160; Earlier application for a public business entity is prohibited.&#160; The Company anticipates that the adoption of this ASU will not have a material impact on its consolidated financial statements.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In June&nbsp;2014, the FASB issued ASU 2014-12, &#147;Compensation - Stock Compensation (Topic 718):&#160; Accounting for Share-Based Payments When the Terms of an Award Provide That a Performance Target Could be Achieved after the Requisite Service Period.&#148;&#160; The amendments in this ASU require that a performance target that affects vesting and that could be achieved after the requisite service period be treated as a performance condition.&#160; A reporting entity should apply existing guidance in Topic 718 as it relates to awards with performance conditions that affect vesting to account for such awards.&#160; This ASU is effective for annual periods, and interim periods within those annual periods, beginning after December&nbsp;15, 2015.&#160; Earlier adoption is permitted.&#160; ASU 2014-12 may be adopted either (a)&nbsp;prospectively to all awards granted or modified after the effective date or (b)&nbsp;retrospectively to all awards with performance targets that are outstanding as of the beginning of the earliest annual period presented in the financial statements, and to all new or modified awards thereafter.&#160; If retrospective transition is adopted, the cumulative effect of applying this update as of the beginning of the earliest annual period presented in the financial statements</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p align="center" style="font-size:10.0pt;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">F-</font>15<a name="PB_15_152458_8912"></a></p>

<br clear="all" style="page-break-before:always;">
<div style="font-family:Times New Roman;">
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;"><a href="#TableOfContents" title="Click to go to Table of Contents">Table of Contents</a></font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">should be recognized as an adjustment to the opening retained earnings balance at that date.&#160; The Company anticipates that the adoption of this ASU will not have a material impact on its consolidated financial statements.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In August&nbsp;2014, the FASB issued ASU 2014-13, &#147;Consolidation (Topic 810): Measuring the Financial Assets and the Financial Liabilities of a Consolidated Collateralized Financing Entity.&#148;&#160; This ASU applies to entities that meet the following criteria:</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="font-size:10.0pt;margin:0in 0in .0001pt 1.0in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">1.</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font>they are required to consolidate a collateralized entity under the Variable Interest Entities guidance;</p>
<p style="font-size:10.0pt;margin:0in 0in .0001pt 1.0in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">2.</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font>they measure all of the financial assets and the financial liabilities of that consolidated collateralized financing entity at fair value in the consolidated financial statements based on other FASB rules; and</p>
<p style="font-size:10.0pt;margin:0in 0in .0001pt 1.0in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">3.</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font>those changes in fair value are reflected in earnings.</p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Under ASU 2014-13, entities that meet these criteria are provided an alternative under which they can choose to eliminate the difference between the fair value of financial assets and financial liabilities of a consolidated collateralized financing entity.&#160; If that alternative is not elected, then ASU 2014-13 indicates that the fair value of the financial assets and the fair value of the financial liabilities of the consolidated collateralized financing entity should be measured in accordance with ASC 820,&#160; &#147;Fair Value Measurement,&#148; and differences between the fair value of the financial assets and the financial liabilities of that consolidated collateralized financing entity should be reflected in earnings and attributed to the reporting entity in the consolidated statement of income or loss.&#160; The amendments in this ASU are effective for annual periods, and interim periods within those annual periods, beginning after December&nbsp;15, 2015. Early adoption is permitted as of the beginning of an annual period.&#160; The Company anticipates that the adoption of this ASU will not have a material impact on its consolidated financial statements.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In August&nbsp;2014, the FASB issued ASU 2014-14, &#147;Receivables - Troubled Debt Restructurings by Creditors (Subtopic 310-40): Classification of Certain Government - Guaranteed Mortgage Loans upon Foreclosure.&#148;&#160; The amendments in this ASU require that a mortgage loan be derecognized and that a separate other receivable be recognized upon foreclosure if the following conditions are met:</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="font-size:10.0pt;margin:0in 0in .0001pt 1.0in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">1.</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font>the loan has a government guarantee that is not separable from the loan before foreclosure;</p>
<p style="font-size:10.0pt;margin:0in 0in .0001pt 1.0in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">2.</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font>at the time of foreclosure, the creditor has the intent to convey the real estate property to the guarantor and make a claim on the guarantee, and the creditor has the ability to recover under that claim; and</p>
<p style="font-size:10.0pt;margin:0in 0in .0001pt 1.0in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">3.</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font>at the time of foreclosure, any amount of the claim that is determined on the basis of the fair value of the real estate is fixed.</p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="font-size:10.0pt;margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman"><font style="font-size:10.0pt;">Upon foreclosure, the separate other receivable should be measured based on the amount of the loan balance (principal and interest) expected to be recovered from the guarantor.&#160; The amendments in</font>  </font>this ASU are effective for annual periods, and interim periods within those annual periods, beginning after December&nbsp;15, 2014.&#160; The Company anticipates that the adoption of this ASU will not have a material impact on its consolidated financial statements.</p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In August&nbsp;2014, the FASB issued ASU 2014-15, &#147;Presentation of Financial Statements &#151; Going Concern (Subtopic 205-40).&#148;&#160; The amendments in this ASU provide guidance about management&#146;s responsibility to evaluate whether there is substantial doubt about an entity&#146;s ability to continue as a going concern or to provide related footnote disclosures.&#160; The amendments require management to assess an entity&#146;s ability to continue as a going concern by incorporating and expanding upon certain principles that are currently in U.S. auditing standards.&#160; Specifically, the amendments (1)&nbsp;provide a definition of the term substantial doubt, (2)&nbsp;require an evaluation every reporting period including interim periods, (3)&nbsp;provide principles for considering the mitigating effect of management&#146;s plans, (4)&nbsp;require certain disclosures when substantial doubt is alleviated as a result of consideration of management&#146;s plans, (5)&nbsp;require an express statement and other disclosures when substantial doubt is not alleviated, and (6)&nbsp;require an assessment for a period of one year after the date that the financial statements are issued (or available to be issued).&#160; The amendments in</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p align="center" style="font-size:10.0pt;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">F-</font>16<a name="PB_16_152513_3531"></a></p>
<div style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><hr size="3" width="100%" noshade align="left" style="color:#010101;"></div>
</div>

<br clear="all" style="page-break-before:always;">
<div style="font-family:Times New Roman;">
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;"><a href="#TableOfContents" title="Click to go to Table of Contents">Table of Contents</a></font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">this ASU apply to all entities and are effective for the annual period ending after December&nbsp;15, 2016, and for annual periods and interim periods thereafter. Early application is permitted.&#160; The adoption of this guidance is not expected to have an impact on the Company&#146;s results of operations or financial position.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In August&nbsp;2014, the FASB issued ASU 2014-16, &#147;Derivatives and Hedging (Topic 815).&#148;&#160; The objective of this ASU is to eliminate the use of different methods in practice and thereby reduce existing diversity under GAAP in the accounting for hybrid financial instruments issued in the form of a share.&#160; The amendments in this ASU apply to all entities that are issuers of, or investors in, hybrid financial instruments that are issued in the form of a share.&#160; The amendments in this ASU do not change the current criteria in GAAP for determining when separation of certain embedded derivative features in a hybrid financial instrument is required.&#160; The amendments clarify how current GAAP should be interpreted in evaluating the economic characteristics and risks of a host contract in a hybrid financial instrument that is issued in the form of a share.&#160; Specifically, the amendments clarify that an entity should consider all relevant terms and features, including the embedded derivative feature being evaluated for bifurcation, in evaluating the nature of the host contract.&#160; Furthermore, the amendments clarify that no single term or feature would necessarily determine the economic characteristics and risks of the host contract.&#160; Rather, the nature of the host contract depends upon the economic characteristics and risks of the entire hybrid financial instrument.&#160; In addition, the amendments in this ASU clarify that, in evaluating the nature of a host contract, an entity should assess the substance of the relevant terms and features when considering how to weight those terms and features.&#160; Specifically, the assessment of the substance of the relevant terms and features should incorporate a consideration of (1)&nbsp;the characteristics of the terms and features themselves, (2)&nbsp;the circumstances under which the hybrid financial instrument was issued or acquired, and (3)&nbsp;the potential outcomes of the hybrid financial instrument, as well as the likelihood of those potential outcomes.&#160; The amendments in this ASU are effective for public entities for fiscal years, and interim periods within those fiscal years, beginning after December&nbsp;15, 2014.&#160; Early adoption is permitted.&#160; The adoption of this guidance is not expected to have an impact on the Company&#146;s results of operations or financial position.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="font-size:10.0pt;margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In November&nbsp;2014, the FASB issued ASU 2014-17, &#147;Business Combinations (Topic 805): Pushdown Accounting.&#148;&#160; The amendments in this ASU provide guidance on whether and at what threshold an acquired entity that is a business or nonprofit activity may elect to apply pushdown accounting in its separate financial statements upon a change-in-control event in which an acquirer obtains control of the acquired entity.&#160; The amendments in this ASU are effective on November&nbsp;18, 2014.&#160; After the effective date, an acquired entity can make an election to apply the guidance to future change-in-control events or to its most recent change-in-control event.&#160; However, if the financial statements for the period in which the most recent change-in-control event occurred already have been issued or made available to be issued, the application of this guidance would be a change in accounting principle.&#160; The </font>Company anticipates that the adoption of this ASU will not have an impact on the Company&#146;s results of operations or financial position.</p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><u><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">NOTE 3 - INVESTMENTS IN AVAILABLE-FOR-SALE SECURITIES</font></u></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Debt securities have been classified in the consolidated balance sheets according to management&#146;s intent.&#160; The amortized cost and their approximate fair values are as follows:</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Management conducts, at least on a quarterly basis, a review of its investment securities to determine if the value of any security has declined below its amortized cost and whether such decline represents other-than-temporary impairment.&#160; The investments in the Company&#146;s investment portfolio that are temporarily impaired as of September&nbsp;30, 2014 consist of 6 debt securities issued by U.S. Government federal agencies, 14 mortgage-backed securities, and one taxable municipal security.&#160; The unrealized loss at September&nbsp;30, 2014 is attributable to changes in market interest rates since the Company acquired the securities.&#160; As management has the ability and the intent to hold debt securities until recovery to cost basis, the declines are deemed to be not other-than-temporary.</font></p>

<div style="font-family:Times New Roman;">
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;"><a href="#TableOfContents" title="Click to go to Table of Contents">Table of Contents</a></font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><u><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Credit Quality Information</font></u></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company utilizes an eight grade internal loan rating system for commercial real estate, construction and commercial loans as follows:</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Loans rated 1 - 4:&#160; Loans in these categories are considered &#147;pass&#148; rated loans and conform in all respects to Company and regulatory requirements.&#160; These are also loans for which no repayment risk has been identified.&#160; Credit or collateral exceptions are minimal, are in the process of correction and do not represent significant risk.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Loans rated 5:&#160; Loans in this category are considered &#147;special mention&#148; and are fundamentally sound, but exhibit potentially unwarranted credit risk or other unsatisfactory characteristics.&#160; The likelihood of loss to the Company is remote.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Loans rated 6:&#160; Loans in this category are considered &#147;substandard&#148; and are inadequately protected by current sound net worth, paying capacity of the obligor, or the value of pledged collateral. Loans in this category also include those loans with unsatisfactory characteristics indicating higher levels of risk.&#160; The combination of one or more of these characteristics increases the possibility of loss to the Company.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Loans rated 7:&#160; Loans in this category are considered &#147;doubtful.&#148;&#160; Loans in this category exhibit weaknesses inherent in the substandard classification and, in addition, collection or liquidation in full is highly questionable.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Loans rated 8:&#160; Loans in this category are considered uncollectible (&#147;loss&#148;) and of such little value that their continuance as an active asset is not warranted.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">On an annual basis, or more often if needed, the Company formally reviews the ratings on all commercial real estate, construction and commercial loans.&#160; For all residential real estate and consumer loans, the Company initially assesses credit quality based upon the borrower&#146;s ability to service the debt and subsequently monitors these loans based upon the borrower&#146;s payment activity.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Loans serviced for others are not included in the accompanying consolidated balance sheets.&#160; As of September&nbsp;30, 2014 and 2013 the unpaid principal balances of loans serviced for others were $32,604,000 and $26,574,000, respectively.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In 2014 and 2013, the Company capitalized mortgage servicing rights totaling $118,000 and $210,000, respectively, and amortized $76,000 and $68,000, respectively.&#160; The balance of capitalized mortgage servicing rights included in other assets at September&nbsp;30, 2014 and 2013 was $289,000 and $240,000, respectively.&#160; The fair value of the Company&#146;s mortgage servicing rights at September&nbsp;30, 2014 and 2013 was $388,000 and $289,000, respectively.&#160; Following is an analysis of the aggregate changes in the valuation allowance for mortgage servicing rights for the years ended September&nbsp;30:</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">As of September&nbsp;30, 2014, the interest rates on FHLB advances ranged from .18% to 2.16% with a weighted-average interest rate of .90%.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Amortizing advances are being repaid in equal monthly payments and are being amortized from the date of the advance to the maturity date on a direct reduction basis.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Borrowings from the FHLB are secured by a blanket lien on qualified collateral, consisting primarily of loans with first mortgages secured by one-to-four family properties.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Deferred tax assets as of September&nbsp;30, 2014 have not been reduced by a valuation allowance because management believes that it is more likely than not that the full amount of deferred tax assets will be realized.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">As of September&nbsp;30, 2014, the Company has federal net operating loss carryovers of approximately $159,000 which expire between 2033 and 2034.&#160; The Company also has $20,000 of alternative minimum tax credit carryovers which do not expire.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The federal income tax reserve for loan losses at the Company&#146;s base year amounted to approximately $1,100,000.&#160; If any portion of the reserve is used for purposes other than to absorb losses for which established, approximately 150% of the amount actually used (limited to the amount of the reserve) would be subject to taxation in the fiscal year in which used.&#160; As the Company intends to use the reserve only to absorb loan losses, a deferred income tax liability of approximately $439,000 has not been provided.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">It is the Company&#146;s policy to provide for uncertain tax positions and the related interest and penalties based upon management&#146;s assessment of whether a tax benefit is more likely than not to be sustained upon examination by tax authorities.&#160; As of September&nbsp;30, 2014, there were no material uncertain tax positions related to federal and state income tax matters.&#160; The Company is currently open to audit under the statute of limitations by the Internal Revenue Service and state taxing authorities for the years ended September&nbsp;30, 2011 through September&nbsp;30, 2014.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;"><a href="#TableOfContents" title="Click to go to Table of Contents">Table of Contents</a></font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><u><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">NOTE 10 - EMPLOYEE BENEFITS</font></u></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company has a <i>401(k)</i> plan which provides for voluntary contributions by participating employees ranging from one percent to seventy-five percent of their compensation, subject to certain limitations.&#160; The Company matches 100% of employee contributions up to a maximum of 5% of participant&#146;s compensation.&#160; Total expense recorded by the Company for the years ended September&nbsp;30, 2014 and 2013 amounted to $72,000 and $76,000, respectively.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company and the Bank entered into a three-year employment agreement (Agreement) with an executive officer.&#160; The Agreement provides for a three-year term, subject to annual renewal by the boards of directors for an additional year beyond the then-current expiration date.&#160; The Agreement also provides for participation in incentive compensation and other employee benefits as described in the Agreement.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Under the terms of the Agreement, upon the occurrence of a change in control, as defined in the Agreement, followed by executive termination of employment, the Company shall pay the executive a lump sum cash payment equal to two times his base salary then in effect and average bonus paid during the two years prior to the change in control; and continued health and life insurance coverage for 24 months.&#160; If at the time of a change in control the remaining term of the Agreement is less than one year, then the term will automatically extend for a period of one year after the date of the change in control.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Bank entered into two-year change in control agreements (Agreements) with an executive officer and an officer.&#160; Under the Agreements, if the employment of the executive officer or the officer is terminated for any reason other than cause as defined in the Agreements or if the executive officer or officer terminates employment for &#147;good reason,&#148; in either case in connection with or within one year of a change in control and the executive officer or officer is not offered a comparable position with the successor company, the executive officer and/or the officer will receive a lump sum payment equal to two times his base salary then in effect and continued coverage under health and life insurance coverage for 24 months.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><u><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">NOTE 11 - EMPLOYEE STOCK OWNERSHIP PLAN (&#147;ESOP&#148;)</font></u></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Bank has adopted a tax-qualified employee stock ownership plan (&#147;ESOP&#148;) for the benefit of eligible employees.&#160; Effective November&nbsp;19, 2012, the Bank converted from a Massachusetts-chartered mutual co-operative bank to a Massachusetts-chartered stock co-operative bank and become the wholly-owned subsidiary of the Company.&#160; The Company completed its initial public offering in connection with the conversion transaction by selling a total of 661,250 shares of common stock at a purchase price of $10.00 per share in a subscription offering, of which 27,700 shares were purchased by the Bank&#146;s ESOP.&#160; The ESOP acquired an additional 18,587 shares in the open market subsequent to the conversion.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The ESOP funded its stock purchase through a loan from the Company equal to 100% of the aggregate purchase price of the common stock. The ESOP trustee will repay the loan principally through the Bank&#146;s contributions to the ESOP and, possibly, dividends paid on common stock held by the plan over the loan term of 6.1 years.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The trustee holds the shares purchased in a loan suspense account and will release the shares from the suspense account on a pro rata basis as it repays the loan. The trustee will allocate the shares released among active participants on the basis of each active participant&#146;s proportional share of compensation for the plan year. Generally, participants will receive distributions from the ESOP upon separation from service. The trustee will reallocate any unvested shares of common stock forfeited by participants upon their separation from service among the remaining participants in the plan.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Under applicable accounting requirements, the Company will record a compensation expense for the ESOP equal to the fair market value of the shares when they are committed to be released from the suspense account to participants&#146; accounts under the plan.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">At September&nbsp;30, 2014, the remaining principal balance on the ESOP debt was $409,000 and the number of shares held by the ESOP was 46,287.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p align="center" style="font-size:10.0pt;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">F-</font>27<a name="PB_27_145037_5137"></a></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><u><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">NOTE 12 - EQUITY INCENTIVE PLAN</font></u></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Shareholders of Meetinghouse Bancorp,&nbsp;Inc. approved the 2014 Equity Incentive Plan (&#147;Plan&#148;) on February&nbsp;9, 2014, and the Board of Directors ratified the vote on April&nbsp;15, 2014.&#160; The total number of shares that can be awarded in the Plan is 92,575.&#160; The number of restricted stock awards that can be granted is 26,450 and the number of options that can be granted is 66,125.&#160; The Board of Directors granted stock awards on August&nbsp;19, 2014 in the amount of 18,519 shares to its management, employees and directors.&#160; For the year ended September&nbsp;30, 2014, compensation expense applicable to the stock awards was $13,000 with a related tax benefit of $4,000.&#160; Unrecognized compensation expense for non-vested restricted stock totaled $221,000 as of September&nbsp;30, 2014, which will be recognized over the remaining weighted-average vesting period of 2.9 years.&#160; As of September&nbsp;30, 2014, there were no forfeitures of stock awards granted.&#160; As of September&nbsp;30, 2014, there were no options granted under the Plan.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><u><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">NOTE 13 - FINANCIAL INSTRUMENTS</font></u></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company is party to financial instruments with off-balance sheet risk in the normal course of business to meet the financing needs of its customers.&#160; These financial instruments include commitments to extend credit.&#160; Those instruments involve, to varying degrees, elements of credit and interest rate risk in excess of the amount recognized in the balance sheet.&#160; The contract or notional amounts of those instruments reflect the extent of involvement the Company has in particular classes of financial instruments.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company&#146;s exposure to credit loss in the event of nonperformance by the other party to the financial instrument for commitments to extend credit is represented by the contractual notional amount of those instruments.&#160; The Company uses the same credit policies in making commitments and conditional obligations as it does for on-balance sheet instruments.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p align="center" style="font-size:10.0pt;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">F-</font>28<a name="PB_28_145228_2159"></a></p>
<div style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><hr size="3" width="100%" noshade align="left" style="color:#010101;"></div>

<div style="font-family:Times New Roman;">
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;"><a href="#TableOfContents" title="Click to go to Table of Contents">Table of Contents</a></font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Commitments to extend credit are agreements to lend to a customer as long as there is no violation of any condition established in the contract.&#160; Commitments generally have fixed expiration dates or other termination clauses and may require payment of a fee.&#160; The Company evaluates each customer&#146;s creditworthiness on a case-by-case basis.&#160; The amount of collateral obtained, if deemed necessary by the Company upon extension of credit, is based on management&#146;s credit evaluation of the borrower.&#160; Collateral held varies but usually includes income producing commercial properties or residential real estate.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Standby letters of credit are conditional commitments issued by the Company to guarantee the performance by a customer to a third party.&#160; The credit risk involved in issuing letters of credit is essentially the same as that involved in extending loan facilities to customers.&#160; As of September&nbsp;30, 2014 and 2013, the maximum potential amount of the Company&#146;s obligation was $149,000 for financial and standby letters of credit.&#160; The Company&#146;s outstanding letters of credit generally have a term of less than one year.&#160; If a letter of credit is drawn upon, the Company may seek recourse through the customer&#146;s underlying line of credit.&#160; If the customer&#146;s line of credit is also in default, the Company may take possession of the collateral, if any, securing the line of credit.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Notional amounts of financial instrument liabilities with off-balance sheet credit risk are as follows as of September&nbsp;30:</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><u><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">NOTE 15 - FAIR VALUE MEASUREMENTS</font></u></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">ASC 820-10, &#147;Fair Value Measurement - Overall,&#148; provides a framework for measuring fair value under generally accepted accounting principles.&#160; This guidance also allows an entity the irrevocable option to elect fair value for the initial and subsequent measurement for certain financial assets and liabilities on a contract-by-contract basis.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In accordance with ASC 820-10, the Company groups its financial assets and financial liabilities measured at fair value in three levels, based on the markets in which the assets and liabilities are traded and the reliability of the assumptions used to determine fair value.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Level 1 - Valuations for assets and liabilities traded in active exchange markets, such as the New York Stock Exchange.&#160; Level 1 also includes U.S. Treasury, other U.S. Government and agency mortgage-backed securities that are traded by dealers or brokers in active markets.&#160; Valuations are obtained from readily available pricing sources for market transactions involving identical assets or liabilities.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Level 2 - Valuations for assets and liabilities traded in less active dealer or broker markets.&#160; Valuations are obtained from third party pricing services for identical or comparable assets or liabilities.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Level 3 - Valuations for assets and liabilities that are derived from other methodologies, including option pricing models, discounted cash flow models and similar techniques, are not based on market exchange, dealer, or broker traded transactions.&#160; Level 3 valuations incorporate certain assumptions and projections in determining the fair value assigned to such assets and liabilities.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">A financial instrument&#146;s level within the fair value hierarchy is based on the lowest level of input that is significant to the fair value measurement.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">A description of the valuation methodologies used for instruments measured at fair value, as well as the general classification of such instruments pursuant to the valuation hierarchy, is set forth below.&#160; These valuation methodologies were applied to all of the Company&#146;s financial assets and financial liabilities carried at fair value for September&nbsp;30, 2014 and 2013.&#160; The Company did not have any significant transfers of assets between levels 1 and 2 of the fair value hierarchy during the years ended September&nbsp;30, 2014 and 2013.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company&#146;s cash instruments are generally classified within level 1 or level 2 of the fair value hierarchy because they are valued using quoted market prices, broker or dealer quotations, or alternative pricing sources with reasonable levels of price transparency.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company&#146;s investment in mortgage-backed securities and other debt securities available-for-sale is generally classified within level 2 of the fair value hierarchy.&#160; For these securities, we obtain fair value measurements from </font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p align="center" style="font-size:10.0pt;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">F-</font>30<a name="PB_30_145513_6175"></a></p>
<div style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><hr size="3" width="100%" noshade align="left" style="color:#010101;"></div>
</div>

<br clear="all" style="page-break-before:always;">
<div style="font-family:Times New Roman;">
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;"><a href="#TableOfContents" title="Click to go to Table of Contents">Table of Contents</a></font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">independent pricing services.&#160; The fair value measurements consider observable data that may include dealer quotes, market spreads, cash flows, the U.S. treasury yield curve, trading levels, market consensus prepayment speeds, credit information and the instrument&#146;s terms and conditions.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Level 3 is for positions that are not traded in active markets or are subject to transfer restrictions, valuations are adjusted to reflect illiquidity and/or non-transferability, and such adjustments are generally based on available market evidence.&#160; In the absence of such evidence, management&#146;s best estimate is used.&#160; Subsequent to inception, management only changes level 3 inputs and assumptions when corroborated by evidence such as transactions in similar instruments, completed or pending third-party transactions in the underlying investment or comparable entities, subsequent rounds of financing, recapitalization and other transactions across the capital structure, offerings in the equity or debt markets, and changes in financial ratios or cash flows.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company&#146;s impaired loans are reported at the fair value of the underlying collateral if repayment is expected solely from the collateral.&#160; Collateral values are estimated using level 2 inputs based upon appraisals of similar properties obtained from a third party.&#160; The fair value of impaired loans estimated using level 3 inputs are based on management estimates.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The following summarizes assets measured at fair value on a recurring basis as of September&nbsp;30:</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><u><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">NOTE 17 - OTHER COMPREHENSIVE INCOME (LOSS)</font></u></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Accounting principles generally require that recognized revenue, expenses, gains and losses be included in net income.&#160; Although certain changes in assets and liabilities are reported as a separate component of the stockholders&#146; equity section of the consolidated balance sheets, such items, along with net income, are components of comprehensive income.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><u><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">NOTE 18 - REGULATORY CAPITAL</font></u></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Bank is subject to various regulatory capital requirements administered by the federal banking agencies.&#160; Failure to meet minimum capital requirements can initiate certain mandatory and possibly additional discretionary actions by regulators that, if undertaken, could have a direct material effect on the Bank&#146;s financial statements.&#160; Under capital adequacy guidelines and the regulatory framework for prompt corrective action, the Bank must meet specific capital guidelines that involve quantitative measures of the Bank&#146;s assets, liabilities and certain off-balance sheet items as calculated under regulatory accounting practices.&#160; The Bank&#146;s capital amounts and classification are also subject to qualitative judgments by the regulators about components, risk weightings and other factors.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Quantitative measures established by regulation to ensure capital adequacy require the Bank to maintain minimum amounts and ratios (set forth in the table below) of total and Tier 1 capital (as defined in the regulations) to risk-weighted assets (as defined), and of Tier 1 capital (as defined) to average assets (as defined).&#160; Management believes, as of September&nbsp;30, 2014 and 2013, that the Bank meets all capital adequacy requirements to which it is subject.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">As of September&nbsp;30, 2014, the most recent notification from the Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation categorized the Bank as well capitalized under the regulatory framework for prompt corrective action.&#160; To be categorized as well capitalized the Bank must maintain minimum total risk-based, Tier 1 risk-based and Tier 1 leverage ratios as set forth in the table.&#160; There are no conditions or events since that notification that management believes have changed the institution&#146;s category.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><u><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">NOTE 20 - CONDENSED PARENT COMPANY ONLY FINANCIAL STATEMENTS</font></u></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The following are the condensed balance sheets, statements of operations and cash flows for Meetinghouse Bancorp,&nbsp;Inc. (&#147;Parent Company&#148;) as of and for the years ended September&nbsp;30:</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
